clue.text: Pin colours to the mast

parts.note: a regiment's or ship's colours are its flag
a pole is a mast or upright spar

explanation.surface: A defiant gesture: nailing one's colours to the mast and refusing to give in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pin' is not a verb here: in golf the pin is the flagstick marking the hole.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf the pin is the slim staff carrying a small flag that marks where the hole is.

clue.text: Special terms, requiring shelter in storms? On the contrary

this reverses the stated arrangement, so the storms go inside the shelter instead

parts.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
gales are storms

explanation.surface: A sailor asks about the special terms for seeking shelter during storms.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue as written puts shelter inside storms; 'On the contrary' says the reverse arrangement is the one wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal jargon is the special vocabulary of lawyers, a set of terms outsiders struggle with.

clue.text: Traveller could be blotto and regret 3 disturbance

indicators.note: a disturbance throws things into disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A drunken traveller wakes up blotto and full of regret after a commotion.
explanation.walkthrough: The '3' is a stray mark from the scanned page and plays no part; 'could be' is the link.
explanation.definitionFit: A globetrotter is someone who travels widely around the world, a keen traveller.

clue.text: Exposed without legal remedy and proscribed me proscribed

definitions.meaning: historically an outlaw was put outside the law's protection, with no recourse to the courts

explanation.walkthrough: The repeated 'me proscribed' is a scrap duplicated in scanning and is not part of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To outlaw a person once meant removing all legal protection; to outlaw a thing means to ban it.

clue.text: Qualified girl showed way round Bolivian capital

indicators.note: the girl and the guide go round, placing them either side of the Bolivian letter

parts.note: Ena is a girl's name, a crossword regular
led means guided or showed the way

indicators.note: a capital letter here is the first letter of the word Bolivian

explanation.surface: A trained girl guided tourists around the Bolivian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bolivian capital' suggests La Paz or Sucre but means only its first letter, B.
explanation.definitionFit: Being enabled means being made able or qualified to do something.

clue.text: Assemblage that often floored the Romans in Britain

definitions.text: Assemblage that often floored the Romans in Britain

parts.words: Assemblage that often floored the Romans in Britain
parts.note: floored reads as stunned, but means covered the floors of Roman villas with a pattern of small assembled tiles

explanation.walkthrough: 'Floored' looks like defeated, as if the Britons beat the Romans; it means paved.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman villas in Britain commonly had floors made of tiny coloured tiles assembled into pictures.

clue.text: Godly song taken from a pithy mnemonic

indicators.note: the answer is a run of letters lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A religious chant drawn from a short memory aid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a song of praise to God, sung in worship.

clue.text: Valets curse such habits

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's man, so valets are men
to swear is to curse

explanation.surface: Gentlemen's servants damn their masters' clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Habits' suggests behaviour but means clothing, as in a monk's habit.
explanation.definitionFit: Habits here are garments, and clothing for men is the kind valets look after.

clue.text: The peony is chancy for the beginner .

indicators.note: something chancy is random, so these letters fall into a haphazard order

explanation.surface: Growing peonies is risky for a novice gardener.
explanation.definitionFit: A neophyte is a newcomer or novice, someone just starting out.

clue.text: In the past, I pocketed commission

indicators.note: pocketed means put inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ago means in the past

explanation.surface: An agent admits to having taken a cut on a deal years back.
explanation.definitionFit: An agio is a fee or premium charged for exchanging currency, a banker's commission.

clue.text: They reduce friction in conduct between dances

indicators.note: between means placed inside, with the dances either side

parts.note: balls are formal dances
bearing is one's conduct or deportment

explanation.surface: Good behaviour at dances keeps social friction down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ball bearings are small steel balls in machinery that let parts turn with little friction.

clue.text: Present to get better of old wife

explanation.surface: Advice on how to outdo an elderly spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to present something as a gift or honour.

clue.text: With spade, discover neckcloth right away in river

indicators.note: in means the trimmed neckcloth sits inside the river's name

parts.note: a cravat is a neckcloth

explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes the letter for right from the neckcloth; the Exe is a river in Devon, south-west England.

clue.text: Watches live clinches in wrestling

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
holds are grips used by wrestlers

explanation.surface: A fan watches live wrestling, full of clinches.
explanation.definitionFit: To behold is to see or watch, an old-fashioned verb of looking.

clue.text: Bachelor always on time for a drink

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
ever means always
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A single man who is always on time for a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A beverage is any drink other than water.

clue.text: One who makes an institution collapse

definitions.meaning: someone who establishes a school, firm or society
to fall in or sink, as a building or ship does

explanation.definitionFit: Founder as a noun is an establisher of an institution; as a verb it means to collapse or sink.

clue.text: Area from which the house cannot be The winn seen

definitions.text: Area from which the house cannot be The winn seen

parts.words: Area from which the house cannot be The winn seen
parts.note: house means theatre audience: the wings and backstage, out of sight of the auditorium

explanation.walkthrough: 'The winn' is a fragment from the next column of the page and plays no part. 'House' suggests a dwelling but is the theatre audience.
explanation.definitionFit: In a theatre, the part of the building hidden from the audience lies beyond the visible acting area.

clue.text: One leaving garment I had to alter

indicators.note: to alter is to change, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tailor had a garment to change before someone's departure.
explanation.definitionFit: An emigrant is a person leaving their country to settle elsewhere.

clue.text: Keeping block mostly on anger

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to stop is to block
rage is anger

explanation.surface: Someone tries largely to suppress their temper.
explanation.definitionFit: Storage is the keeping of goods somewhere for later use.

clue.text: Garment not quite the match intended, say

indicators.note: not quite means falling short by a letter, so the last one goes

parts.note: a vesta is an old name for a short wax match

indicators.note: say signals that a word is to be heard rather than spelt

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a garment does not quite match what they had in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: A vesta is a short wax match; 'not quite' cuts it to VEST, and 'say' gives MENT for MEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestment is a ceremonial robe, especially one worn by clergy, so a garment.

clue.text: Morally committed to attack

definitions.meaning: a French loan describing a writer or artist devoted to a political or moral cause
to ... the enemy is to attack them in battle

explanation.definitionFit: Engagé is a borrowed word for politically committed; engage as a verb means join battle with.

clue.text: Expression of approval, receiving endless opulent material

parts.note: fab, short for fabulous, is slang praise

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is removed

parts.note: rich means opulent

explanation.surface: A rich buyer praises sumptuous cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric is cloth or material.

clue.text: Erratic forger caught out and thrown into the cooler

indicators.note: out says the letter for caught is removed from the pool
thrown means the remaining letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: An unreliable counterfeiter is arrested and thrown into prison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooler' is slang for prison, but here means a fridge. Remove C from ERRATIC FORGER and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A refrigerator is an appliance that keeps food cold, quite literally a cooler.

clue.text: Beat in mounted game

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word reads upwards

parts.note: golf is a game

explanation.definitionFit: To flog is to beat with a whip or stick.

clue.text: Perjuror gives backing to fence

indicators.note: backing means the word fence's synonym is read from the end

parts.note: a rail is a fence

explanation.surface: A false witness supports a receiver of stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fence' suggests a receiver of stolen goods, fitting the perjuror, but is RAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A perjuror lies under oath, so is by definition a person telling untruths.

clue.text: Simpleton finding giant fruit

parts.note: a goose is a silly person

explanation.surface: A fool comes across an enormous piece of fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: Gooseberry is called a 'goosegog' in British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A goosegog is a colloquial British word for a gooseberry, a fruit.

clue.text: Time in its entirety, perhaps

parts.note: all of time with no beginning or end, endless duration

explanation.definitionFit: Eternity is infinite time, the whole of time without limit.
